# Lerngesellschaft / Learning Society

> A Basel association supporting children's curiosity and learning through personal accompaniment, public science and classroom activities. Its three programmes are Lernbus, Forscherbühne and Gehirn und Gesellschaft. The current German and English websites share one canonical domain, lerngesellschaft.ch. learningsociety.ch redirects to the English homepage.

## Current association

Contact: team@jonashertner.com
Address: Münsterplatz 17, 4051 Basel, Switzerland.

## Preserved essay: relational learning

Jonas Hertner's 2026 manifesto grew out of tutoring in Zurich. It is preserved as a dated, standalone essay; it is not the current Basel programme description. The historical author, place and essay text remain unchanged.

- [Essay, German](https://lerngesellschaft.ch/essays/relational-learning/de/): Web edition with sidenotes.
- [Essay, English](https://lerngesellschaft.ch/essays/relational-learning/en/): Parallel composition.
- [German print edition](https://lerngesellschaft.ch/essays/relational-learning/de/print/): A5 book preview; save as PDF in the browser.
- [English print edition](https://lerngesellschaft.ch/essays/relational-learning/en/print/): Same.
- [German Markdown](https://lerngesellschaft.ch/essays/relational-learning/de/paper.md): Plain Markdown source.
- [English Markdown](https://lerngesellschaft.ch/essays/relational-learning/en/paper.md): Same.

## Structure of the white paper

Five movements, building one argument:

1. **Voraussetzung / Premise**: The modern Volksschule took its basic form in the nineteenth century and is not built to resolve every child's individual act of thought. Citing Criblez and the EDK on Swiss schooling history, and Illich, Labaree, Goodman, and Robinson on the institutional logic of schooling.
2. **Der relationale Kern / The Relational Core**: In an age of AI, education must foreground the capacities that require responsibility, relationship, and judgment: relational intelligence. Cites Isabelle C. Hau's SSIR essay "Welcome to the Era of Relational Intelligence" and Werner Jaeger's *Paideia* on the classical conception.
3. **Der entwicklungspsychologische Boden / The Developmental Ground**: Children arrive curious; ordinary school structures often make curiosity risky to express. Cites Susan Engel's work on curiosity in classrooms.
4. **Die Probe des Verstehens / The Test of Understanding**: The Feynman-associated test: explain a thing so that a beginner can understand it. The individual tutoring hour as the ideal site for this test.
5. **Die Praxis / The Practice**: One hour. One child. One table. One sheet of paper. What a tutorial actually consists of, why "homework help" misses the point, what parents can expect.

## Citations

- Susan Engel, *The Hungry Mind: The Origins of Curiosity in Childhood* (Harvard University Press, 2015)
- Susan Engel, "Children's Need to Know: Curiosity in Schools", *Harvard Educational Review* 81/4 (2011), 625–645, DOI 10.17763/haer.81.4.h054131316473115
- Richard Feynman, *The Pleasure of Finding Things Out* (Perseus, 1999); *The Feynman Lectures on Physics* (Addison-Wesley, 1963–1965)
- Werner Jaeger, *Paideia* (3 vols.; De Gruyter, 1934–1947; Oxford University Press English translation, 1939–1944)
- Hans-Georg Gadamer, *Erziehung ist sich erziehen* (Kurpfälzischer Verlag, 2000); "Education Is Self-Education", *Journal of Philosophy of Education* 35/4 (2001)
- Ivan Illich, *Deschooling Society* (1971)
- David F. Labaree, *Someone Has to Fail: The Zero-Sum Game of Public Schooling* (Harvard University Press, 2010)
- Lucien Criblez (ed.), *Bildungsraum Schweiz: Historische Entwicklung und aktuelle Herausforderungen* (Haupt, 2008)
- Ken Robinson, *Out of Our Minds: The Power of Being Creative* (Capstone, 3rd ed. 2017); TED talk *Do schools kill creativity?* (2006)
- Isabelle C. Hau, "Welcome to the Era of Relational Intelligence", *Stanford Social Innovation Review* 24/2 (Spring 2026), DOI 10.48558/PY66-AH68
